claims.text: Advanced computational methods can improve determination of thermodynamic properties in multicomponent high-entropy materials.
Advanced CALPHAD approaches are a suitable intervention for determining the solid-to-fluid transition properties listed in the hypothesis.
Machine-learning models are a suitable intervention for determining the solid-to-fluid transition properties listed in the hypothesis.
CALPHAD can determine multicomponent phase diagrams through mathematical descriptions of Gibbs free energies and diffusion mobilities for each phase.
Advanced computational methods can effectively capture the complex thermodynamic behavior of high-entropy materials.
The proposed methods can capture the effects of lattice distortions.
Static interatomic-length disorder and temperature-driven dynamic lattice distortion affect thermodynamic and structural characteristics of high-entropy solid solutions.
Capturing lattice distortions will improve determination of solid-to-fluid transition temperature, fusion properties, volume change, and dense-fluid heat capacity.
The intervention will improve accuracy relative to current experimental and computational methods.
The intervention will improve computational efficiency relative to current computational methods.
The improved method will determine transition temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, volume change, and dense-fluid heat capacity.
The intervention is applicable across high-temperature states and various compositions.
The approach is limited by the availability of reliable thermodynamic data.
A significant deviation between computational predictions and experimental measurements would falsify the hypothesis.
